items.title: Welcome!
items.details: I'm Anna Grigorescu, a computer science student at UIUC. This gallery (which draws inspiration from my art history minor) is an overview of my experience and projects.

items.title: Google SWE Intern
items.details: Summer 2026. Kotlin, Android, Jetpack Compose, Linux, Version Control, AI. Still completing!
paragraphs: I was an Software Engineering Intern at Google in Summer 2026.
Accomplishments:
achievements: Architected, implemented, and drove the launch of a significant design change to the Android Auto interface that will optimize layouts and provide core action controls. Currently in Alpha, and is in the process of ramping to over 100 million active users.

Authored a comprehensive technical design document outlining architecture, automated testing strategies, and API integration, securing alignment and approval from senior engineers across the organization.
Made 22 changes to production code within the first 2 months of the internship to add features, fix bugs, and reduce technical debt, significantly outpacing the initial project timeline.
Architected and tested new files to create Android Auto easter eggs in Kotlin using agentic workflows, for a team hackathon.

items.title: Google ASDI Intern
items.details: Summer 2025. Kotlin, Linux, Android, Jetpack Compose.
paragraphs: I was an Associate Software Developer Intern at Google in Summer 2025.
Accomplishments:
achievements: Designed and implemented a user-facing feature for the Android Phone App's Calling Card for over 600 million daily active users and over 7 billion daily calls.
Engineered (end-to-end) a transformative feature used for Android's production code, working closely with UX designers and tech leads to iteratively develop a positive user experience.
Gained proficiency with multi-threaded applications, data services, and state management, as well as navigating internal tools and Google's 2 billion line codebase.
Created an internal API accessible across the Android Phone App's teams that will make it easier for applications to support accessibility for Android's ~800 million color blind and low-vision users.

items.title: Research Intern (LUC)
items.details: Summers 2022 and 2024. Python, Linux, Flask, HTML/CSS/JS, Pandas, Git
paragraphs: I was a research intern at Loyola University Chicago the summers after my sophomore and senior years of high school. Accomplishments:
achievements: I developed a Flask web application allowing researchers to evaluate and optimize the efficiency of their computer vision models on a cluster of low-powered devices, facilitating resource-constrained AI development for the eventual goal of running artificial intelligence on phones.
I contributed to a published research paper on the security risks of popular machine learning model hubs such as HuggingFace, bringing awareness to the risks of open-source artificial intelligence.

I evaluated and presented a comparative analysis of leading Python charting libraries, assessing ease of use and visual appeal to guide optimal tool selection for scientific data visualization, which led to changes in the lab's charting methods for their research papers.

items.title: Android Calling Card
items.tags: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Design Docs, Data Services, State Management
items.details: Intern Project. Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Design Docs, Data Services, State Management.
paragraphs: As part of my software engineering internship at Google, I end-to-end engineered a feature for Android's Calling Card.
achievements: Designed and implemented an internal Material Color Utilities API that allows developers to find contrasting text on top of images, making it easier to support accessibility goals for ~800 million colorblind and low-vision users.

Used the utilities API to build contrasting "smart colors" that dynamically match the hue of user images for the Android Calling Card—a feature used by 600 million daily active users and 7 billion daily calls.

Collaborated end-to-end with UX designers and tech leads to navigate Google's multi-billion-line codebase, writing production-level code with a focus on multi-threading, state management, and data services.

items.title: Crop Counter for Brazilian Nonprofit
items.tags: Python, various LLM APIs, Google Sheets scripts
items.details: Project in collaboration with a nonprofit. Python, various LLM APIs, Google Sheets scripts
paragraphs: As a UIUC Grainger Career Scholar, I worked in a group of four to research the viability of using AI to count crops in partnership with Toca, a Brazilian nonprofit supporting family farmers.
achievements: Researched computer vision tools to help family farmers calculate crop volumes independently, eliminating their reliance on third-party pricing metrics.
Evaluated models to handle the irregular shapes of natural castor beans, addressing recognition challenges by incorporating volume-to-area density estimations.
Created a tracking utility that lets organizers input physical batch weights to cross-validate and audit the accuracy of our statistical models.

items.title: National Merit Scholar
items.details: Awarded to ~0.5% of high school seniors each year
paragraphs: To win the award, a student must go through several stages which include qualification, performance and submitting accomplishments. First, a student must qualify by scoring in the top 1% of test takers in their state. Based on these scores, approximately 16,000 students are selected nationally as semifinalists. To advance, they must submit a list of accomplishments, including a high school transcript, a personal essay and a letter of recommendation. Finally, 7,600 students nationwide are chosen as National Merit award winners. Winners receive a $2,500 scholarship along with academic recognition.

items.title: James Scholar
items.details: Selected for the Honors Program within UIUC's Grainger College of Engineering.
paragraphs: "The gifted undergraduate student who is seeking the challenge of advanced and unusual academic opportunities and the maximum freedom in course selection will find such opportunity in the James Scholar Program in Engineering. In addition to the various honors sections, courses, and special educational opportunities made available by the various departments of the college, the program administers several engineering honors courses. These courses are designed to bring together James Scholars from throughout the college to study various interdisciplinary subjects.

The James Scholar Program is voluntary and therefore enrolls superior students who are actively seeking unusual academic challenges. It strives to interact with each student on an individual basis; its foundation lies in the student's interest and academic goals." - Siebel School of Computing and Data Science Website

This means they have qualified as a National Cyber Scholar based on their performance in the CyberStart gamified learning platform, and gone on to complete the 2023 Cyber Foundations Academy, completing the SANS Foundations course and earning the industry-recognized GIAC Foundational Cybersecurity Technologies (GFACT) certification.

These students have shown true excellence in their cybersecurity learning journey. Cybersecurity is a fascinating and challenging field, but not everyone has the tenacity and analytical capacity to be exceptional. They have demonstrated they have what it takes, and that with continued study they could have a place in this industry. All of our Scholars with Honors should be incredibly proud of their achievement." - NCSF Website
